stem:
The mass of one helium atom is $6.64 \times 10^{-27}$ kg.
A balloon contains $2.5 \times 10^{23}$ helium atoms.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Calculate the mass of the helium in the balloon.
Give your answer in kilograms in standard form.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A second balloon contains $4.15 \times 10^{-3}$ kg of helium.
Calculate the total number of helium atoms in the two balloons.
Give your answer in standard form.

syllabus_check: 4052 Numbers: standard form with negative and positive indices, multiplying and dividing numbers in standard form, adding numbers in standard form with the same power, and rewriting a result in standard form ($16.6 \times 10^{-4} \to 1.66 \times 10^{-3}$; $0.625 \times 10^{24} \to 6.25 \times 10^{23}$). All values exact: $6.64 \times 2.5 = 16.6$ and $4.15 \div 6.64 = 0.625$.
originality_note: A single physical context (helium atoms in two balloons) drives a multiply-then-normalise part and a divide-then-add part, with a negative index throughout; not a population table, not a plain 'write in standard form', not a calculator-then-convert pair. Shares no context or numbers with the exemplars or with Q1-Q6 of this paper.
